title: Guwahati Nightclub Horror: Video Shows Woman Stripped, Assaulted By Bouncers
excerpt: A viral video shows a woman being stripped and beaten by bouncers at 'The Locals' disco club in Guwahati's Khanapara area; accounts of what triggered the violence conflict, and Guwahati Police have registered a case and opened an investigation.
body:
• A viral video shows a woman with almost no clothes on being kicked and beaten by bouncers in the basement of 'The Locals' disco club in Khanapara, Guwahati, on Thursday night.
  • Local reports say she was stripped and dragged from the club on the building's fourth floor down to the basement; her identity has not been established.
  • Pratidin Time has reported a conflicting account — that the woman, who was drunk, hit a female bouncer with a beer bottle first — which neither the police nor the club has confirmed.
  • Guwahati Police have registered a case and opened an investigation; no official statement has been issued so far.

Video Captures Assault In Club Basement

A disturbing video circulating on social media appears to show a young woman being stripped, dragged, and beaten by bouncers at a nightclub in Guwahati, Assam, in what is shaping into one of the most shocking alleged cases of violence against women in the Northeast in recent years. The incident occurred on Thursday night at 'The Locals' disco club in the Khanapara area of the city, according to multiple media reports including NDTV.

In the video, the woman is seen lying on the ground in the basement of the building with almost no clothes on her body, while a bouncer kicks her. Another sequence shows a female bouncer kicking her as well, even as a woman attempts to lift her from the floor. Several men are visible in the frame; none of them appear to intervene.

Local news outlets reported that the victim was stripped and dragged on the fourth floor of the building, where the nightclub is housed, and then brought down to the basement in that state. The incident came to light after a local media person reached the basement and alerted others. When reporters later went to the fourth floor, they found the club's gate locked and its lights switched off, according to the reports.

"In the video, the woman is seen lying on the ground in the basement of the building with almost no clothes on her body, while a bouncer kicks her."

Conflicting Accounts Of What Triggered The Violence

What set off the confrontation remains disputed, and no account has been independently verified. While NDTV, Hub News, and nktv.in have reported that the bouncers stripped and assaulted the woman, Pratidin Time has carried a conflicting version: that the intoxicated woman struck a female bouncer with a beer bottle first and was subsequently beaten in the parking lot.

The reason for the fight has yet to be ascertained, and the woman's identity has not been established. Neither the club's management nor Guwahati Police has issued an official statement on what transpired. Guwahati Police have registered a case and initiated an investigation, Northeast Today reported, but further details are awaited.

The divergence between the two accounts — and the fact that the trigger is still unknown — means the precise sequence of events can only be established by the police investigation, including any available CCTV footage from the club and the building.

Echoes Of The 2012 Guwahati Molestation Case

The case has revived memories of the July 2012 Guwahati molestation case, when a teenage girl was allegedly molested and manhandled by a crowd of around 30 men outside a city bar — an attack that lasted nearly half an hour and was filmed. That case drew national outrage, led to arrests based on video footage, and put Guwahati's nightlife and its media ethics under a harsh spotlight.

Fourteen years on, the pattern is painfully familiar: a young woman in a nightlife setting, a camera capturing the assault, and bystanders who did not step in. The 2012 case ended with convictions, including that of the prime accused Amar Jyoti Kalita, and prompted a high-power committee of the Gauhati High Court to recommend tighter regulation of bars and wine shops in the city. Whether this week's incident leads to similar institutional consequences for club security practices remains to be seen.

What It Means For The Diaspora

For members of the diaspora — especially women visiting Guwahati or with family there — the episode is a grim reminder that nightlife safety in parts of India remains precarious, and that private security staff in clubs can themselves become a source of danger. It is worth watching whether Assam's authorities move beyond a single investigation to review how bouncers at city venues are vetted and supervised.

What's Next

The immediate question is whether Guwahati Police will identify the woman and the bouncers seen in the video, and whether arrests follow. Investigators are expected to examine CCTV footage from the club and the building's basement to establish the sequence of events — including whether the woman was assaulted after striking a bouncer, as Pratidin Time reported, or whether the attack was unprovoked, as other outlets have alleged.

Attention will also fall on the club's management, which shut its gates and turned off its lights when reporters arrived — a move that is likely to draw scrutiny. Any findings on how a paying customer ended up stripped and beaten inside a licensed venue could force a reckoning for Guwahati's nightlife industry, much as the 2012 case did for its bars.
